text:
maria: Quick question — should we standardize our internal RPCs on gRPC + protobufs or keep REST/JSON at the edge? Thinking about gateway complexity, client compatibility, telemetry, quotas, and rollout UX.
kevin: +1 for gRPC internally. Binary protos give smaller payloads, stricter contracts, and language codegen makes client/server iterate faster.
nora: Concern: browser clients and external integrators. grpc-web + envoy works but adds another moving part. If we insist on gRPC-only, we'll need a solid strategy for external JSON, docs, and sample clients.
linus: Observability note: our Console assumes HTTP status + path-based dashboards. gRPC uses grpc-status/trailers and :method names like "POST /package.Service/Method". We can map those, but need to normalize method -> route in our telemetry pipeline.
sam: Quotas and rate-limiting: Envoy supports gRPC method-level matching, but current quota service expects URL paths. If we go gRPC we must ensure method-to-route mapping so billing & quota work per-feature.
maria: Also rollout UX: we want per-method canary/A-B rollouts. gRPC + envoy can do traffic splitting by header or cluster, but our console currently expects path-based rules. Need mapping layer or extend the Console to understand gRPC methods.
kevin: Proposal: Protobufs for schemas + gRPC for internal RPCs. At the edge we expose a JSON REST facade using an auto-generated gRPC-gateway (proto -> OpenAPI + JSON mapping). That keeps internal perf & types while preserving external compatibility.
nora: +1 but proto JSON mapping has gotchas (enums, google.protobuf.Timestamp, repeated fields). We must publish canonical JSON examples and generate OpenAPI so SDKs for non-gRPC consumers are straightforward.
sam: Operations checklist: ensure per-method metrics (latency, qps), per-method quota enforcement, and per-method cost attribution. If gateway translates JSON -> gRPC, the gateway must inject a canonical route label that our telemetry picks up.
linus: Example envoy match for method-based routing (rough sketch):
```
# envoy route filter snippet
- match:
    headers:
      - name: ":path"
        exact: "/redwood.api.Inference/Generate"
  route:
    cluster: inference-v2
```
kevin: For browser apps we should evaluate grpc-web vs JSON over REST. grpc-web avoids double translation (json->grpc) but requires client libs. If we opt for gRPC-gateway + CORS + JSON for public APIs, grpc-web becomes optional for internal UI clients.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed proto-schema-service -> prod-internal (traffic 5%) :rocket:
maria: Acceptance criteria draft:
- per-method telemetry surfaces in Console as first-class routes
- quota enforcement supports gRPC method labels and shows up in billing/alerts
- generated OpenAPI + JSON examples for all public proto services
- Console rollout UI can target method-level canaries
kevin: Action items:
- I'll draft RFC with example proto definitions, generated gateway mapping, and rollout flow (PR by EOW)
- Include sample codegen commands and ci job to publish OpenAPI
nora: I'll prototype an OpenAPI generator for our protos and test parity with existing REST samples.
sam: I'll validate quota enforcement in envoy for gRPC matches and run a short load test to confirm metrics pipeline labels survive the gateway.
maria: I'll put a slot on Tues 10am for a follow-up sync. Please drop links in the RFC to any prior gateway configs. Thanks! :pray:
